title: optimize nccl collectives and scheduler to overlap comm/compute for tensor-parallel runtime
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel workloads were spending a non-trivial portion of step time waiting on collectives. This PR implements asynchronous NCCL collectives + scheduler changes to aggressively overlap communication with local compute and to make the runtime tolerant to varying NCCL versions and topology. Approach: add a dedicated communication CUDA stream per device for TP collectives, use non-blocking NCCL APIs where available and fall back to blocking ops with the previous ordering for older NCCL. Introduce a lightweight comm scheduler that issues prefetch all-reduces for KV cache shards and reduction steps ahead of time based on the existing execution plan, and uses CUDA events to synchronize only at necessary points. Also tune NCCL algo selection and P2P thresholds at runtime (heuristics based on tensor size and mesh shape). Integration notes: ties into continuous batching by exposing pre-collective hooks so batch coalescing can initiate comm earlier; KV cache changes ensure shard ownership and prefetch do not race with serving lookups. Results: on internal multi-GPU perf canary tests (TP size=8, seq=1024, batch=4) end-to-end throughput improved 12-25% depending on model size and batch composition; p99 latency improved ~18% for hot-path sequences; network utilization improved and GPU compute utilization increased. Safety and fallbacks: runtime detects NCCL version < 2.12 and disables async path; added assertions and stress tests to prevent deadlock ordering regressions. Testing: unit tests for scheduler logic, multi-GPU integration tests that run on internal nightly GPU pool, and benchmark scripts to reproduce numbers. See files changed for implementation details and small perf docs.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Can you clarify how ordering is maintained between overlapping collectives and the existing compute kernels? There's a risk of data races if events aren't placed correctly.

Arjun Patel: We use a dedicated comm stream and place CUDA events on the compute stream before issuing a comm that depends on the compute result; the comm stream waits on that event. For reductions that feed back into compute we place an event on the comm stream and make compute wait only where absolutely necessary. Added comments and unit tests to validate ordering.
Liam O'Connor: We saw flaky failures on the GPU smoke CI on first run. Is there a fallback if the NCCL async APIs are not stable on some clusters?

Arjun Patel: Yes - runtime probes NCCL version at startup. If version < 2.12 or if a topology probe detects unsupported behavior, the async path is disabled and we use the previous blocking collectives. The CI flakes were due to an environment race in the smoke script; fixed and re-ran.
Priya Nair: Please add a way to force legacy mode via env var for debugging in prod clusters.
Arjun Patel: Added REDWOOD_TP_FORCE_LEGACY_COLLECTIVE=1 override and documented it in docs/perf/nccl_tuning.md.
Maya Chen: Approving after adding more perf numbers and ensuring the canary is green.
Liam O'Connor: Minor nit on header include order; otherwise LGTM.
Priya Nair: Approved (verified perf improvements on nightly pool).
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance by overlapping NCCL communication with local compute, added comm scheduler and KV cache prefetching. Expected throughput gains of 12-25% and p99 latency reductions (~18%) in TP=8 configurations. Fallbacks available for older NCCL versions.
perf_bench_repro: profiling: Nsight Systems and CUPTI traces were used to validate overlap and event ordering
notes: This change touches low-level scheduling; coordinate with infra when rolling to Dedicated and Private clusters.
KV cache prefetch semantics are conservative by default to avoid extra memory pressure; ops team can tune via REDWOOD_TP_PREFETCH_WINDOW.
